NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_acronyms¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_acronyms(const Note& other) const

Acronym-Set Similarity Score Between Two Notes¶

jaccard_acronyms(other) scores each cell pair by the Jaccard index of their acronym sets and returns a shape-preserving Float64 Note of native scores. It is the acronym-set scoring member of the set-similarity family; see also overlap_acronyms and intersect_acronyms.

How the score is computed¶

An acronym is a run of two or more uppercase ASCII letters on a word boundary (NASA, ESA); matches are lowercased and deduplicated into sets A and B. The score is |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|, in [0, 1], symmetric.

A cell with no uppercase letters has an empty acronym set. Both sets empty → 1.0; one empty and one not → 0.0. The default printer shows up to six decimals, trailing zeros trimmed.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Bytes-mode input raises NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_acronyms requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs); a numel mismatch raises NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_acronyms expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Two Of Four Acronyms Shared¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"NASA ESA NOAA"})
                 .nlp().jaccard_acronyms(pluss::make_note({"NASA ESA JAXA"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, dtype=Float64)
[0.5]

Sets {nasa, esa, noaa} and {nasa, esa, jaxa} share two of four distinct acronyms → 0.5.

See Also¶

  • NoteNlpAccessor::overlap_acronyms: the containment score over the same sets.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_acronyms: the shared acronyms themselves.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_tokens / NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_terms / NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_citations / NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_symbols: other set kinds.
